messages.subject: Actiwatch data
parts:
Since the actiwatch csv data can be imported in GGIR, the test dataset (in German), in the Gitub can not be loaded in my R script. Here is the example for my csv directly exported from Actiware(File 1). 

I have seen someone in the discussion group said they can only import the csv without header. I tried again. The problem is GGIR can read their csv documents (File 2) but no mine. I have reformat our test data(File 3) exactly as the one they have upload in the group.  Additionally, when i used File 2, since this file did not include header, R can not recognized the sample rate. I used sf=(60) to define but it doesn't work.

attach my GGIR script.


g.shell.GGIR(
  # General parameters
  datadir = "example",
  outputdir = "output_results",
  dataFormat = "actiwatch_csv",
  extEpochData_timeformat = "%d-%m-%y %H:%M:%S",  
  mode = 1:5,
  f0 = 0,
  f1 = 1,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  do.imp = TRUE,
  idloc = 1,
  print.filename = FALSE,
  storefolderstructure = FALSE,
  do.cal = TRUE,
  do.enmo = TRUE,
  do.anglez = TRUE,
  chunksize = 1,
  printsummary = TRUE,
 
  # Part 1 parameters:
  windowsizes = c(60, 900, 3600),
  do.cal = TRUE,
  do.enmo = TRUE,
  do.anglez = TRUE,
  chunksize = 1,
  printsummary = TRUE,
 
  # Part 2 parameters:
  data_masking_strategy = 1,
  ndayswindow = 7,
  hrs.del.start = 1,
  hrs.del.end = 1,
  maxdur = 9,  # 修正参数名称
  includedaycrit = 16,
  L5M5window = c(0,24),
  M5L5res = 10,
  winhr = c(5,10),
  qlevels = c(1380/1440, 1410/1440),
  qwindow = c(0,24),
  ilevels = c(seq(0, 400, by=50), 8000),
  mvpathreshold = c(100, 120),
 
  # Part 3 parameters:
  timethreshold = c(5,10),
  anglethreshold = 5,
  ignorenonwear = TRUE,
 
  # Part 4 parameters:
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  includenightcrit = 16,
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  loglocation = NULL,  
  outliers.only = FALSE,
  criterror = 4,
  relyonguider = FALSE,
  do.visual = TRUE,
 
  # Part 5 parameters:
  threshold.lig = c(30, 40, 50),
  threshold.mod = c(100, 120),
  threshold.vig = c(400, 500),
  boutcriter = 0.8,
  boutcriter.in = 0.9,
  boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
  boutdur.in = c(10, 20, 30),
  boutdur.lig = c(1, 5, 10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1, 5, 10),
  timewindow = c("WW"),
 
  # Report generation
  do.report = c(2, 4, 5)
)

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Actiwatch data
parts:
Hello Yujiao,

"File 1.csv" works for me with:

GGIR(datadir = ".....",
     outputdir = ".....",
     dataFormat = "actiwatch_csv",
     extEpochData_timeformat = "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S",
     mode = 1:2,
     windowsizes = c(15, 900, 3600), # 15 is the expected epoch length
     HASIB.algo = "Sadeh1994",
     def.noc.sleep = c(),
     overwrite = TRUE,
     do.report = c(2),
     visualreport = FALSE)

Problem 1: You are not specifying the timestamp format correctly. The function probably gave you the error message "Time format in data 23/11/2019 does not match with time format %d-%m-%y %H:%M:%S as specified by argument extEpochData_timeformat, please correct." 

Problem 2: Similarly the epoch length you specified is not correct and GGIR probably gave you the error message: "The short epoch size as specified by the user as the first value of argument windowsizes (60 seconds) does NOT match the short epoch size we see in the data (15 seconds). Please correct."

I coded GGIR to give these error message such that GGIR users can read them and do not have to ask for help because the error message provides all the hints you need.

Best wishes,

Vincent
